evidence.text: A long time after the LORD had given Israel rest from all the enemies around them, when Joshua was old and well along in years,
“and you have seen everything that the LORD your God has done to all these nations for your sake, because it was the LORD your God who fought for you.
The LORD your God will push them out of your way and drive them out before you, so that you can take possession of their land, as the LORD your God promised you.
Instead, you shall hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.
The LORD has driven out great and powerful nations before you, and to this day no one can stand against you.
One of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised.
Therefore watch yourselves carefully, that you love the LORD your God.

know for sure that the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations before you. Instead, they will become for you a snare and a trap, a scourge in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the LORD your God has given you.

Now behold, today I am going the way of all the earth, and you know with all your heart and soul that not one of the good promises the LORD your God made to you has failed. Everything was fulfilled for you; not one promise has failed.

But just as every good thing the LORD your God promised you has come to pass, likewise the LORD will bring upon you the calamity He has threatened, until He has destroyed you from this good land He has given you.

If you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you will quickly perish from this good land He has given you.”

c: Joshua

Joshua, son of Nun, was Moses’ assistant and successor as Israel’s leader. Joshua brought the young nation across the Jordan River into the Promised Land of Canaan, faithfully following God’s leadership.
Before Israel reached Mount Sinai, Joshua led Israel’s warriors when Amalek attacked Israel (
). Shortly thereafter, he was among the twelve men Moses sent to scout the Promised Land (
). Against popular opinion, Joshua and Caleb urged Israel to occupy Canaan immediately (
), and as a result, of the twelve spies, only they entered Canaan (
God directed Moses to designate Joshua as his successor (
). After Moses died, Joshua led Israel across the Jordan River (
) to the conquest of Jericho (
). When Israel suffered defeat at Ai, Joshua turned to the Lord and followed his instructions to purge Israel of sin (
); then Israel conquered Ai (
). Following God’s instructions to Moses (
), Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal (
) and read the blessings and curses of the covenant (
). Joshua conducted campaigns against two coalitions of Canaanite kings, a southern and a northern coalition (
). Joshua’s victories in these campaigns opened the hill country to settlement by the Israelites.
After supervising the allotment of territories to the tribes of Israel, Joshua received his own portion in the land of Ephraim (
). He established the cities of refuge (
) and the Levitical cities (ch
) and released the 2½ tribes that had settled east of the Jordan River to return home (
). As he grew old, Joshua charged Israel to remain faithful to God (

). His farewell message at Shechem summarized God’s dealings with Israel and concluded with the familiar challenge, “Choose today whom you will serve. . . . But as for me and my family, we will serve the
Lord
). Joshua died at the age of 110 and was buried in Timnath-serah (
Joshua demonstrated exceptional faithfulness throughout his life, except in dealing with the Gibeonites (
), when he neglected to consult the Lord regarding a decision. Israel served God faithfully under Joshua and the elders Joshua trained (
). Stephen mentions Joshua in his martyr’s sermon (
), and the writer of Hebrews uses Joshua’s conquest of Jericho as an illustration of faith (
). It is fitting that Joshua and Jesus are the same name in Hebrew: Joshua led Israel into physical salvation in Canaan; Jesus leads all who believe in him into eternal salvation.

God fights for you:

be very careful to love:
Love is a function of will and intention. Emotion and attraction are the results, not the essence, of love. Because love is (or is not) willed, love can be commanded but not coerced.

Apostasy—turning away from the true God—is fatal. • Because God is holy, Joshua could speak with optimism regarding God’s promises and the good land into which God had brought them. God will not change his holy character even if his people change. The rebellion of God’s people cannot damage his holiness, but rebellion will destroy those who rebel.

will no longer drive them out:
If Israel associated with the Canaanite remnant, God would oblige the Israelites by not driving out that remnant. God ultimately gives people what they seek.
